stem: You have a dataset of emails each already labeled spam or not spam, and you want to train a model to predict that label for new emails. Which type of machine learning is this?
explanationCorrect: The training data carries known labels (spam or not spam) and the goal is to predict that label on new inputs, which is the defining setup of supervised learning.
explanationIncorrect: Unsupervised learning works on data without labels and tries to find structure on its own, such as grouping similar items, so it does not fit a problem where every example already has the answer. Reinforcement learning trains an agent by rewarding or penalizing actions it takes in an environment over time; there is no environment or reward signal here, just labeled examples. Clustering is a specific unsupervised technique for grouping unlabeled data, so it is the wrong paradigm for label prediction. Learning a mapping from labeled examples to a target label is supervised learning.

stem: Which statement best describes the relationship between artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, and generative AI?

options.text: They are nested: AI is the broadest field, machine learning is a subset of AI, deep learning is a subset of machine learning, and generative AI is built on deep learning
They are four unrelated fields with no overlap
Generative AI is the broadest field and contains artificial intelligence
Machine learning and artificial intelligence are two names for exactly the same thing

explanationCorrect: The terms nest from broad to narrow: AI is the umbrella, machine learning is one way to achieve AI, deep learning is a subset of ML using neural networks, and generative AI is a deep-learning application that creates new content.
explanationIncorrect: They are clearly related, not unrelated fields. Generative AI is a narrow, recent branch, not the broadest category that contains AI. Machine learning is one approach within AI, not a synonym for all of AI, since AI also includes techniques that are not learned from data. The correct picture is the nested hierarchy from AI down to generative AI.

stem: You want to predict a house's sale price, a continuous numeric value, from its features. Which kind of supervised learning task is this?
explanationCorrect: Predicting a continuous number such as a price is a regression task, where the model outputs a value along a range rather than a discrete label.
explanationIncorrect: Classification predicts a discrete category (such as spam or not spam), not a continuous number. Clustering is unsupervised and groups unlabeled data; it does not predict a target value. Reinforcement learning trains an agent through rewards in an environment and does not fit a labeled price-prediction problem. Predicting a continuous value is regression.

stem: You have unlabeled customer data and want to discover natural groupings of similar customers without predefined categories. Which approach fits?
explanationCorrect: With no labels and the goal of finding structure, clustering (an unsupervised technique) groups similar records together so natural segments emerge from the data itself.
explanationIncorrect: Supervised classification and regression both require labeled examples to learn a target, which you do not have here. Reinforcement learning optimizes an agent's actions against a reward signal, not grouping of static unlabeled records. Discovering groups in unlabeled data is unsupervised clustering.

stem: A model has already been trained and is now returning predictions for new incoming data in production. What is this phase called?
explanationCorrect: Using a trained model to produce predictions on new data is inference; it is the serving phase that follows training.
explanationIncorrect: Training is the earlier phase where the model learns its parameters from data, which has already happened here. Feature engineering is the preparation of input variables before training. Data labeling is annotating examples with target values for supervised training. Producing predictions from a finished model is inference.

stem: A model scores very high on its training data but performs poorly on new, unseen data. What does this most likely indicate?
explanationCorrect: Overfitting is exactly this pattern: the model has memorized the training data, including its noise, so it generalizes poorly to data it has not seen.
explanationIncorrect: Underfitting is the opposite, where the model is too simple and does poorly even on the training data. Inference hardware affects speed and cost, not the gap between training and test accuracy. Output size is unrelated to generalization. Strong training performance with weak generalization is overfitting.

stem: Which AWS service is the managed platform for building, training, and deploying your own custom machine learning models at scale?
explanationCorrect: Amazon SageMaker is the end-to-end managed ML platform for building, training, tuning, and deploying custom models, covering the full model lifecycle.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon Bedrock provides access to pre-built foundation models for generative AI; it is not where you build and train your own custom models from data. Amazon Polly is a text-to-speech service. Amazon Textract extracts text and data from documents. The custom-model build-and-train platform is Amazon SageMaker.

stem: An agent learns to play a game by receiving rewards for good moves and penalties for bad ones, improving through trial and error. Which type of machine learning is this?
explanationCorrect: Reinforcement learning trains an agent through rewards and penalties as it takes actions in an environment, learning a policy by trial and error, which is exactly the game-playing setup described.
explanationIncorrect: Supervised learning maps labeled inputs to outputs and has no reward signal. Unsupervised learning finds structure in unlabeled data, again with no rewards. Transfer learning reuses a pre-trained model on a new task; it is not a reward-driven trial-and-error paradigm. Reward-and-penalty learning is reinforcement learning.

stem: You need to create a large, high-quality labeled dataset for supervised training using human labelers. Which AWS service manages data-labeling workflows?
explanationCorrect: SageMaker Ground Truth orchestrates data-labeling jobs, including human labeling workforces and automated assistance, to build high-quality training datasets.
explanationIncorrect: SageMaker Clarify measures bias and explainability, not labeling. Amazon Bedrock provides foundation models for generative AI. Amazon Polly is text-to-speech. Managed labeling is SageMaker Ground Truth.

stem: For a fraud detector, failing to catch an actual fraud is very costly, so you want to maximize the share of real frauds the model detects. Which metric captures this goal?

options.text: Recall, the fraction of actual positives the model correctly identifies
Precision, the fraction of positive predictions that are correct

explanationCorrect: Recall measures how many of the true frauds were caught, so maximizing recall minimizes missed frauds, which is the priority when a false negative is the costly outcome.
explanationIncorrect: Precision measures how many flagged items were truly fraud; optimizing it reduces false alarms but does not directly minimize missed frauds. Latency and throughput are performance metrics of the serving system, not detection quality. Catching more of the real frauds is recall.

stem: Free-form text, images, and audio are examples of which kind of data, which foundation models are especially good at handling?
explanationCorrect: Text, images, and audio lack a fixed tabular schema, so they are unstructured data, the kind foundation models are particularly effective at processing and generating.
explanationIncorrect: Structured tabular data, relational schema data, and normalized database rows all describe organized rows and columns with a defined schema, which is not what free-form text, images, and audio are. That content is unstructured data.

stem: In supervised learning, the input variables the model learns from are called features. What is the known target value it learns to predict called?
explanationCorrect: In supervised learning the target the model is trained to predict is the label, paired with the input features in each training example.
explanationIncorrect: A hyperparameter is a training configuration value like learning rate, not the prediction target. A gradient is used to update weights during training. An epoch is one pass over the training data. The predicted target is the label.

stem: Which AWS service gives you access to foundation models from providers such as Anthropic, Meta, and Amazon through a single API, without provisioning or managing any model infrastructure?
explanationCorrect: Amazon Bedrock is the fully managed service that exposes foundation models from multiple providers behind one API, so you can call them for text or image generation without standing up any infrastructure.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon Rekognition is a purpose-built computer vision service for detecting objects, faces, and text in images and video; it is not a gateway to general foundation models. Amazon Comprehend is a managed natural language service for tasks like sentiment analysis and entity extraction, not a catalog of generative foundation models. AWS Glue is a serverless data integration and ETL service and has nothing to do with model inference. The single-API, multi-provider foundation model service is Amazon Bedrock.

stem: You want a generative AI assistant to answer questions using your company's internal documents, keeping answers grounded in that private data, without retraining or fine-tuning the underlying model. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), retrieving relevant documents and supplying them as context to the model
Continuously pre-training the model on the public internet
Raising the model's temperature so it invents more answers

explanationCorrect: RAG retrieves the most relevant passages from your document store at query time and passes them to the model as context, so answers are grounded in your private data with no model retraining.
explanationIncorrect: Pre-training the model further on the public internet neither incorporates your private documents nor is something a practitioner does casually; it is expensive and does not target your data. Raising the temperature makes outputs more random and actually increases the chance of ungrounded, made-up answers, which is the opposite of what you want. Reducing the context window gives the model less room to read supplied material, hurting grounded answering. The technique that grounds a model in private data without retraining is Retrieval Augmented Generation.

stem: You are deploying a generative AI chat feature and must block certain harmful topics and filter unsafe content in both prompts and responses. Which Amazon Bedrock capability is purpose-built for this?
explanationCorrect: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock let you define denied topics and content filters that are applied to both user prompts and model responses, which is exactly the responsible-use control described.
explanationIncorrect: Provisioned Throughput reserves model capacity for predictable, high-volume inference; it is a performance and cost feature, not a safety filter. Bedrock Agents orchestrate multi-step tasks by calling tools and APIs on the model's behalf; they coordinate actions rather than screen content for harm. Fine-tuning adapts a model to your data and style, but it is not a reliable topic or safety filter and does not give you configurable denied topics. The capability for content filtering and blocked topics is Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: Your security team asks whether prompts and completions sent to a foundation model in Amazon Bedrock are used to train the base models or exposed outside your account. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Bedrock does not use your prompts or completions to train the base foundation models, and your data is encrypted in transit and at rest within your account boundary
Bedrock adds all prompts to a shared public dataset that anyone can query
Bedrock requires you to email prompts to each model provider for processing
Bedrock stores your prompts unencrypted by default and shares them with other customers

explanationCorrect: Amazon Bedrock does not use your inputs or outputs to train its base foundation models, and it encrypts your data in transit and at rest, keeping it within your account, which is what a security review needs to confirm.
explanationIncorrect: Bedrock does not publish your prompts to any shared or public dataset; that would directly contradict its data-isolation model. It also does not require emailing data to providers; inference happens through the managed service API within AWS. And it does not store your data unencrypted or share it with other customers; encryption at rest and in transit is applied and data stays isolated to your account. The accurate statement is that Bedrock keeps your data private, encrypted, and out of base-model training.

stem: What is a foundation model?

options.text: A large model pre-trained on broad, unlabeled data that can be adapted to many downstream tasks
A small model trained to perform exactly one narrow task
A rules engine built entirely from hand-written if-then logic
A database that stores cached answers to look up

explanationCorrect: A foundation model is trained once on a broad corpus and can then be applied or adapted to many tasks (summarization, Q&A, generation), which is what makes it foundational.
explanationIncorrect: A model built for a single narrow task is a traditional task-specific model, the opposite of a broadly applicable foundation model. A hand-coded rules engine is not a learned model at all. A cache of answers is a lookup table, not a model that generalizes. A foundation model is the broadly pre-trained, widely adaptable model.

stem: Large language models process text as sequences of which unit, which also drives context limits and per-request pricing?

options.text: Tokens, which are pieces of words

explanationCorrect: LLMs break text into tokens (subword pieces), and the number of tokens determines how much fits in the context window and how much a request costs.
explanationIncorrect: Pixels are the unit of images, not text for a language model. Models do not treat paragraphs as indivisible units; they subdivide text into tokens. Gigabytes measure memory, not the linguistic unit a model consumes. The unit is the token.

stem: You want a model's responses to be more deterministic and focused rather than creative and varied. Which inference parameter do you lower?

options.text: The number of tokens in your prompt

explanationCorrect: Temperature controls randomness in generation: lowering it makes the model favor the most probable next tokens, producing more focused and repeatable output.
explanationIncorrect: Prompt length changes how much context the model has, not how random its sampling is. The parameter count is a fixed property of the model you cannot tune per request. The Region affects where inference runs, not output randomness. The randomness control is temperature.

stem: To find documents semantically similar to a query, you convert text into numeric vectors that place similar meanings close together in vector space. What are these vectors called?
explanationCorrect: Embeddings are dense numeric vectors that capture meaning, so semantically similar text ends up near each other, which is what powers semantic search and retrieval.
explanationIncorrect: Tokens are the subword units of input text, not the meaning vectors used for similarity. Hyperparameters are training configuration values like learning rate. Gradients are values used to update weights during training. The similarity vectors are embeddings.

stem: A model can only consider a limited amount of input text at once when generating a response. What is this limit called?
explanationCorrect: The context window is the maximum amount of text (measured in tokens) a model can take into account at once, bounding how much prompt and history it can use.
explanationIncorrect: The learning rate is a training hyperparameter that controls step size, unrelated to input length at inference. Batch size is how many examples are processed together during training. Epoch count is how many passes over the training data occur. The input-length limit is the context window.

stem: Which AWS service is a generative-AI-powered assistant for business and, in its developer form, for coding and answering AWS questions?
explanationCorrect: Amazon Q is AWS's generative-AI assistant, offered for business use and in a developer variant that helps with coding and AWS-specific questions.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon Athena is a serverless SQL query service over data in S3. Amazon Kinesis handles real-time streaming data. Amazon Neptune is a graph database. The generative-AI assistant is Amazon Q.

stem: You take an existing foundation model and train it further on your own labeled domain data to specialize its behavior. What is this called?

options.text: Pre-training a new model from scratch

explanationCorrect: Fine-tuning continues training a pre-trained model on your own data so it adapts to a specific domain or task without the cost of training from scratch.
explanationIncorrect: Pre-training from scratch builds a model from the ground up on massive data, which is far more expensive and not what adapting an existing model means. Inference is using a finished model to make predictions, not training it. Tokenization is splitting text into tokens. Specializing an existing model on your data is fine-tuning.

stem: Besides temperature, which inference parameter limits sampling to the smallest set of most-likely tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds a threshold?
explanationCorrect: Top-p, or nucleus sampling, restricts the model to the smallest group of top tokens whose probabilities add up to the threshold, controlling diversity by probability mass.
explanationIncorrect: Maximum tokens caps output length, not which tokens are eligible. Epochs and learning rate are training-time settings, not inference sampling controls. The cumulative-probability sampling control is top-p.

stem: Which model type generates images from text prompts, as in Amazon Titan Image Generator or Stable Diffusion?
explanationCorrect: Text-to-image generation is done by diffusion-based models, which iteratively turn noise into an image conditioned on the text prompt.
explanationIncorrect: A text-to-speech model produces audio, not images. A tabular regression model predicts numbers from structured data. A speech-to-text model transcribes audio. Image generation from text uses a diffusion-based text-to-image model.

stem: You want to give a chat model persistent instructions about its role and tone that apply across the whole conversation. Which prompt element is designed for this?
explanationCorrect: The system prompt sets high-level, persistent instructions (role, tone, constraints) that frame the whole conversation, separate from individual user messages.
explanationIncorrect: Temperature controls randomness, not instructions. An embedding is a numeric vector representation of text, not a directive. A stop sequence tells the model where to stop generating. Persistent role and tone guidance is the system prompt.

stem: Which AWS offering lets you quickly prototype generative AI apps in a low-code, playground-style environment built on Amazon Bedrock?
explanationCorrect: PartyRock is a hands-on, low-code playground built on Amazon Bedrock for quickly building and experimenting with generative AI apps without deep setup.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse. AWS Snowball moves large data physically. Amazon Neptune is a graph database. The generative AI prototyping playground is PartyRock.

stem: Which are examples of Amazon's own family of foundation models available through Amazon Bedrock?

options.text: Amazon Titan and Amazon Nova models

explanationCorrect: Amazon Titan and Amazon Nova are Amazon's own foundation model families offered in Amazon Bedrock alongside third-party models.
explanationIncorrect: Aurora and Redshift are databases. EC2 and EBS are compute and block storage. SQS and SNS are messaging services. Amazon's own foundation models are Titan and Nova.

stem: You include several examples of the desired input-and-output pattern directly in the prompt so the model follows that pattern. What is this technique called?
explanationCorrect: Providing a handful of worked examples in the prompt is few-shot prompting; the model infers the pattern from those examples at inference time without any weight changes.
explanationIncorrect: Fine-tuning changes the model's weights by training on data; few-shot happens purely in the prompt with no training. Pre-training builds the base model on massive data up front. RLHF is a training-time alignment method using human preference data. Putting examples in the prompt is few-shot prompting.

stem: You ask a model to perform a task using only an instruction, with no examples provided. What is this called?
explanationCorrect: Giving only an instruction and no examples is zero-shot prompting; the model relies entirely on what it learned during pre-training to perform the task.
explanationIncorrect: Few-shot prompting includes example pairs, which this does not. Fine-tuning is additional training on data, not a prompting style. Data augmentation expands a training dataset with transformed samples and is unrelated to how you phrase a single prompt. An instruction with no examples is zero-shot.

stem: You want a managed way to implement RAG on Bedrock: ingest your documents, chunk and embed them, store the vectors, and retrieve relevant context at query time. Which Bedrock feature provides this end to end?
explanationCorrect: Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock is the managed RAG capability: it handles ingestion, chunking, embedding, vector storage, and retrieval, so you get grounded answers without building the pipeline yourself.
explanationIncorrect: Provisioned Throughput reserves dedicated model capacity; it does not build a retrieval pipeline. Amazon Polly is text-to-speech. AWS Batch runs batch compute jobs and is unrelated to retrieval-augmented generation. The managed RAG feature is Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock.

stem: You need a generative AI application to break a request into steps and call external APIs or functions to complete a task, such as looking up an order and then issuing a refund. Which Bedrock capability orchestrates this?
explanationCorrect: Agents for Amazon Bedrock plan a task into steps and invoke the APIs or functions you provide, letting the model take actions rather than only generate text.
explanationIncorrect: Embeddings turn text into vectors for similarity; they do not orchestrate multi-step actions. Temperature tuning adjusts output randomness. Model evaluation compares model quality. The capability that plans steps and calls tools is Agents for Amazon Bedrock.

stem: Your knowledge base changes daily and answers must always reflect the latest documents. Between RAG and fine-tuning, which is generally the better fit, and why?

options.text: RAG, because it retrieves the current documents at query time without retraining the model
Fine-tuning, because you should retrain the model every day on the new documents
Neither; only adjusting temperature keeps answers current
Fine-tuning, because documents baked into the weights stay fresh automatically

explanationCorrect: RAG pulls the latest documents at query time, so new content is reflected immediately with no retraining, which suits a knowledge base that changes daily.
explanationIncorrect: Retraining or fine-tuning every day is slow, costly, and impractical for daily churn. Temperature only affects randomness, not what facts the model can access. Facts baked into weights are frozen at training time and do not update themselves, so fine-tuning is the opposite of fresh. For frequently changing data, RAG is the fit.

stem: You want to compare two foundation models on your task before choosing one, using both automatic metrics and human review. Which Amazon Bedrock capability supports this?
explanationCorrect: Bedrock model evaluation lets you compare models on your data using automatic metrics and human-based evaluation, which is how you choose the right model for a task.
explanationIncorrect: Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity; it does not measure quality. Guardrails filter unsafe content rather than benchmark models. Knowledge Bases implement retrieval, not evaluation. The comparison feature is model evaluation.

stem: Model responses are being cut off too short. Which inference parameter most directly controls the maximum length of the generated output?
explanationCorrect: The maximum output tokens parameter caps how many tokens the model may generate, so raising it lets responses run longer before being truncated.
explanationIncorrect: Temperature changes randomness, not length. Top-p changes which tokens are sampled by cumulative probability, again affecting variety rather than the length cap. Embedding dimension is a property of vector representations, unrelated to generation length. The length cap is the maximum output tokens setting.

stem: For a high-volume, latency-sensitive, and relatively simple classification prompt, which model choice is usually most appropriate?

options.text: A smaller, faster, cheaper model that is sufficient for the task
Always the largest, most expensive model regardless of the task
A text-to-image model repurposed for text classification
No model at all; classify by hand in a spreadsheet

explanationCorrect: Model selection balances cost, latency, and accuracy: for a simple, high-volume task a smaller and faster model that meets the accuracy bar is the economical, responsive choice.
explanationIncorrect: Defaulting to the largest model wastes money and adds latency when a simpler task does not need it. A text-to-image model is the wrong modality for classifying text. Manual classification does not scale to high volume. The appropriate choice is the smallest capable model.

stem: You want an application that accepts an image and answers questions about its contents in text. What kind of foundation model do you need?

options.text: A multimodal model that accepts image input and produces text output

explanationCorrect: Answering questions about an image requires a multimodal model that can take images as input and generate text, combining vision understanding with language output.
explanationIncorrect: A text-only LLM cannot see an image. A text-to-speech model converts text to audio and does not analyze images. An embeddings-only model produces vectors, not conversational text answers. The task needs a multimodal (image-to-text) model.

stem: A generative model confidently produces a fluent answer that is factually wrong and not grounded in any real source. What is this behavior called?
explanationCorrect: A hallucination is a confident but ungrounded, factually incorrect output; recognizing and mitigating it (for example with RAG and human review) is a core responsible-AI concern.
explanationIncorrect: Overfitting describes a model that memorizes training data and generalizes poorly; it is a training issue, not a fabricated answer. Latency is response time. Quantization is a technique to shrink a model's numeric precision for efficiency. A confident wrong answer is a hallucination.

stem: A hiring model recommends mostly one demographic because its historical training data reflected past biased decisions. Which responsible-AI concern does this illustrate?

options.text: Bias and fairness, arising from biased training data

explanationCorrect: When a model learns from biased historical data it can reproduce and amplify that bias, which is a fairness problem that responsible-AI practices aim to detect and mitigate.
explanationIncorrect: Latency is response speed and unrelated to skewed outcomes. Token limits bound input and output length, not fairness. Cold-start time is an operational delay when a resource initializes. Discriminatory outcomes learned from data are a bias and fairness concern.

stem: AWS publishes documents describing an AI service's intended use cases, limitations, and responsible-AI considerations to improve transparency. What are these called?
explanationCorrect: AWS AI Service Cards are transparency documents that describe an AI service's intended uses, limitations, and responsible-AI design choices, helping customers use the service appropriately.
explanationIncorrect: IAM policies grant permissions; they are not transparency documentation. CloudFormation templates define infrastructure as code. Trusted Advisor checks give cost and best-practice recommendations. The responsible-AI transparency documents are AI Service Cards.

stem: For a high-stakes use case such as a medical or loan decision, which practice best reduces the risk of harmful automated errors?

options.text: Keep a human in the loop to review and approve model outputs before they take effect
Remove all human oversight to make decisions faster
Set temperature to the maximum for more creative decisions
Disable all logging to protect privacy

explanationCorrect: A human-in-the-loop review for high-stakes decisions catches errors and inappropriate outputs before they cause harm, which is a central responsible-AI safeguard.
explanationIncorrect: Removing oversight increases the risk of unchecked harmful decisions in exactly the situations that most need review. Maximizing temperature makes outputs more random, which is dangerous for consequential decisions. Disabling logging removes the audit trail you need for accountability. The safeguard is keeping a human in the loop.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: You must ensure that only specific applications and roles can invoke a given Amazon Bedrock model. Which AWS mechanism enforces that?

options.text: IAM policies granting least-privilege permissions on the Bedrock invoke actions
Security groups attached to the model
A CAPTCHA challenge on every request
Making the model publicly accessible to everyone

explanationCorrect: Access to Bedrock actions is controlled by IAM: least-privilege policies scoped to the invoke actions (and specific models) determine which principals may call the model.
explanationIncorrect: Security groups are network firewalls for resources like EC2 instances; they do not gate who may call a managed model API. A CAPTCHA is a human-verification widget, not an AWS authorization mechanism. Making the model public is the opposite of restricting access. Authorization is enforced with IAM policies.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: For governance you need an audit trail of who made Amazon Bedrock API calls and when. Which service records these management events?
explanationCorrect: AWS CloudTrail records API activity across AWS services, including Bedrock, giving you the who-did-what-and-when audit trail that governance requires.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon Polly is text-to-speech and records no cross-service audit trail. AWS Lambda runs code; it is not an auditing service. Amazon Lex builds conversational bots. The API audit-logging service is AWS CloudTrail.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: Your compliance policy requires that traffic to Amazon Bedrock not traverse the public internet. Which feature keeps that traffic on the AWS network?

options.text: An interface VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) for Bedrock

explanationCorrect: An interface VPC endpoint powered by AWS PrivateLink lets resources in your VPC reach Bedrock privately over the AWS network, so the traffic never crosses the public internet.
explanationIncorrect: A NAT gateway and an internet gateway both exist precisely to route traffic to the public internet, which is what you are trying to avoid. A public S3 bucket is a storage exposure and unrelated to private connectivity. Private access to Bedrock is achieved with an interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink).

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: You want to detect statistical bias in a machine learning model's training data and predictions and to generate explainability reports. Which SageMaker capability provides this?
explanationCorrect: SageMaker Clarify measures bias in data and model predictions and produces feature-importance explainability reports, supporting fairness and transparency governance.
explanationIncorrect: SageMaker Ground Truth is for labeling training data, not detecting bias. Bedrock Provisioned Throughput reserves inference capacity. Amazon Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data such as PII in S3; it is a data-security service, not a model-bias tool. Bias detection and explainability come from SageMaker Clarify.

stem: You ask the model to think step by step and show its reasoning before giving a final answer, which improves accuracy on multi-step problems. Which prompting technique is this?
explanationCorrect: Chain-of-thought prompting asks the model to work through intermediate reasoning steps before the final answer, which tends to improve performance on complex, multi-step tasks.
explanationIncorrect: Zero-shot with no guidance gives only an instruction and does not elicit step-by-step reasoning. Fine-tuning changes model weights through training, not a prompting style. Quantization compresses a model's numeric precision for efficiency. Eliciting explicit reasoning steps is chain-of-thought prompting.

stem: A RAG pipeline needs to store embeddings and search them by similarity efficiently. Which kind of data store is used for this?

options.text: A vector database or vector store, such as Amazon OpenSearch Serverless or Aurora with pgvector

explanationCorrect: RAG stores document embeddings in a vector store that supports similarity search (for example OpenSearch Serverless or Aurora with pgvector), so the most relevant chunks can be retrieved for a query.
explanationIncorrect: A message queue moves messages between components, not similarity search over vectors. A block storage volume is raw disk for an instance. A DNS service resolves names. Embedding similarity search uses a vector database.

stem: You use a foundation model to condense long support tickets into short summaries. This is an example of which common application?
explanationCorrect: Condensing long text into a shorter version that preserves the key points is text summarization, a core generative-AI language task.
explanationIncorrect: Image classification labels images. Speech synthesis turns text into audio. Anomaly detection finds outliers in structured data. Condensing text is summarization.

stem: Your company wants an internal assistant that answers employee questions using connected enterprise data sources such as wikis and documents, while respecting each user's access permissions. Which offering fits?
explanationCorrect: Amazon Q Business is a generative-AI assistant that connects to enterprise data sources and answers questions while honoring the user's access permissions, which suits an internal knowledge assistant.
explanationIncorrect: Amazon Polly is a text-to-speech service that produces audio and does not answer questions over enterprise data. Amazon Kinesis ingests and processes real-time streaming data, not knowledge retrieval. AWS Batch runs batch compute jobs and has no assistant or permission-aware search capability. The permission-aware enterprise knowledge assistant is Amazon Q Business.

stem: You must generate summaries for millions of documents where immediate responses are not needed and cost matters more than latency. Which Amazon Bedrock inference option fits best?

options.text: Synchronous on-demand inference, one call per document
Provisioned Throughput sized for a live chatbot
Fine-tuning a new model for each document

explanationCorrect: Batch inference processes large volumes of prompts asynchronously at lower cost, which fits a bulk, latency-tolerant workload like summarizing millions of documents.
explanationIncorrect: Synchronous on-demand calls per document are optimized for interactivity, not cost at massive scale. Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity for steady low-latency traffic like a chatbot, not one-off bulk jobs. Fine-tuning per document is nonsensical and costly. The cost-efficient bulk option is batch inference.

stem: Stakeholders need to understand why a model produced a particular decision. Which responsible-AI property does this concern?
explanationCorrect: Explainability is the responsible-AI property of being able to understand and communicate why a model produced a given output, which supports trust, debugging, and compliance.
explanationIncorrect: Latency and throughput are performance characteristics, not about understanding decisions. Tokenization is how text is split into tokens. Understanding why a decision was made is explainability.

stem: A public-facing chatbot must avoid producing hateful or harmful content. Which responsible-AI concern and mitigation applies?

options.text: Toxicity and safety, mitigated with content filters or guardrails
Overfitting, mitigated with more training epochs

explanationCorrect: Preventing harmful or hateful output is a toxicity and safety concern, addressed by content filters or guardrails that screen prompts and responses.
explanationIncorrect: Overfitting is a generalization problem unrelated to harmful content. Latency and caching concern speed. Tokenization and embeddings are representation mechanics. Blocking harmful content is a toxicity and safety matter handled by guardrails.

stem: A known risk of generative AI is that users accept its outputs uncritically even when they are wrong. What is this called, and what mitigates it?

options.text: Overreliance (automation bias), mitigated by human review and showing sources and uncertainty
Underfitting, mitigated by using a larger model
Cold start, mitigated by provisioned throughput
Data drift, mitigated by sharding the database

explanationCorrect: Overreliance, or automation bias, is the tendency to trust AI output without scrutiny; it is mitigated by keeping humans in the loop and by surfacing sources and uncertainty so users can judge the output.
explanationIncorrect: Underfitting is a model-capacity problem, not a user-trust behavior. Cold start is an operational latency issue. Data drift is a change in data distribution over time. Uncritical trust in AI output is overreliance.

stem: To reduce biased outcomes from a model, which practice about training data helps most?

options.text: Use diverse, representative training data and check it for bias
Train only on data from one group for consistency
Remove all human oversight from the process

explanationCorrect: Bias often originates in the data, so using diverse, representative data and actively checking it for bias is the most effective way to reduce biased outcomes.
explanationIncorrect: The smallest possible dataset tends to be less representative and can worsen bias. Training on one group's data bakes in a skewed view. Removing oversight makes bias harder to catch. Representative, bias-checked data is the right practice.

stem: A user embeds hidden instructions in input text to make the model ignore its guidelines and behave in unintended ways. What is this attack called?
explanationCorrect: Prompt injection is an attack where crafted input manipulates the model into ignoring its instructions or safeguards, and it is a key safety concern for generative-AI applications.
explanationIncorrect: Overfitting is a training generalization problem. Data labeling is annotating training data. Quantization compresses a model. Manipulating a model through crafted input is prompt injection.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: For auditing and troubleshooting, you want to capture the actual prompts and completions sent through Amazon Bedrock. Which capability records that content?

options.text: Bedrock model invocation logging to CloudWatch Logs and/or Amazon S3
AWS CloudTrail, which records the full prompt and completion text of every call

explanationCorrect: Bedrock model invocation logging captures request and response content (prompts and completions) to CloudWatch Logs or S3, which is what you enable to audit and troubleshoot model usage.
explanationIncorrect: CloudTrail records that an API call happened and its metadata, but it is not designed to store the full prompt and completion content, so it does not meet this need on its own. Secret scanning finds leaked credentials. Dependency review evaluates dependency changes. Capturing prompt and completion content is model invocation logging.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: You want customer-managed keys to encrypt your fine-tuned model artifacts and data at rest in Amazon Bedrock. Which service provides those keys?

options.text: AWS KMS with customer managed keys

explanationCorrect: AWS KMS provides customer managed keys that Bedrock can use to encrypt data and custom model artifacts at rest, giving you control and an audit trail over the keys.
explanationIncorrect: AWS WAF filters malicious web requests and manages no encryption keys. Amazon Route 53 is a DNS and health-checking service. AWS Shield provides DDoS protection. None of them create or manage cryptographic keys. Customer-managed encryption keys for data and model artifacts come from AWS KMS.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: You must prevent a model from returning personally identifiable information (PII) in its responses. Which Amazon Bedrock feature can detect and redact PII?

options.text: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock, using its sensitive information filters

explanationCorrect: Bedrock Guardrails include sensitive information filters that can detect and redact or block PII in prompts and responses, which is exactly the control needed here.
explanationIncorrect: Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity. Model evaluation compares model quality. Knowledge Bases implement retrieval. PII detection and redaction is a Guardrails capability.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: An auditor asks for AWS's compliance certifications (such as SOC and ISO) relevant to your AI workload. Where do you obtain these reports?

options.text: The Amazon Bedrock console's model prompts

explanationCorrect: AWS Artifact is the portal for AWS compliance reports and certifications like SOC and ISO, which auditors need regardless of the workload type.
explanationIncorrect: The Bedrock console runs and configures models; it does not host compliance certifications. Amazon Q is an assistant, not a compliance document store. The billing dashboard shows costs. Compliance reports come from AWS Artifact.

domain: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
stem: Under the shared responsibility model for a managed AI service like Amazon Bedrock, what is the customer typically responsible for?

options.text: How they use the service: their data, access controls (IAM), and handling of prompts and outputs
Maintaining the underlying GPUs and servers

explanationCorrect: With a managed service, AWS secures the underlying infrastructure while the customer is responsible for their data, who can access the service, and how they use it, including how prompts and outputs are handled.
explanationIncorrect: Patching the hosting infrastructure, securing data centers, and maintaining the physical hardware are all AWS's responsibilities under the model. The customer owns their data, access control, and usage of the service.

stem: Which learning paradigm trains a model on labeled examples to predict an output for new inputs?
explanationCorrect: Supervised learning uses input-output pairs with known labels so the model learns a mapping it can apply to unseen inputs, as in classification and regression.
explanationIncorrect: Unsupervised learning works on unlabeled data to find structure such as clusters, so it has no target labels to predict. Reinforcement learning learns from rewards received by taking actions in an environment, not from labeled examples. Federated learning is a training approach that keeps data distributed across devices; it describes where training happens, not the labeled-example paradigm.

stem: A model performs very well on training data but poorly on new data. What is this called?
explanationCorrect: Overfitting occurs when a model memorizes training data, including its noise, and fails to generalize, showing a large gap between training and validation performance.
explanationIncorrect: Underfitting is the opposite: the model is too simple and does poorly even on training data. Regularization is a technique to reduce overfitting, not the problem itself. Normalization rescales feature values to a common range and is a preprocessing step, not the phenomenon of failing to generalize.

stem: You want to group customers into segments without predefined labels. Which type of ML task is this?
explanationCorrect: Clustering is an unsupervised task that groups similar data points together without any predefined labels, which fits segmenting customers by behavior.
explanationIncorrect: Classification assigns items to known, predefined categories, which requires labels you do not have here. Regression predicts a continuous numeric value, not a grouping. Forecasting predicts future values of a time series, which is a different objective from discovering customer segments.

stem: In a classification problem with rare positive cases, why can accuracy be a misleading metric?

options.text: A model predicting the majority class every time can score high accuracy while missing the rare cases
Accuracy cannot be computed for classification

explanationCorrect: With heavy class imbalance, always predicting the common class yields high accuracy yet detects none of the rare positives, so metrics like precision, recall, or F1 are more informative.
explanationIncorrect: Accuracy can absolutely be computed for classification, so that claim is false. Accuracy and precision measure different things and are not always equal. Accuracy is a classification metric, not a regression one, so saying it only applies to regression is incorrect.

stem: What is the purpose of splitting data into training, validation, and test sets?

options.text: To tune on validation data and get an unbiased estimate of performance on the held-out test set
To make training run faster only
To increase the total amount of data

explanationCorrect: The validation set guides model selection and hyperparameter tuning, while the untouched test set gives an unbiased estimate of how the model generalizes to unseen data.
explanationIncorrect: Splitting data is about honest evaluation, not primarily about speed. It does not remove the need for labels; supervised sets still require them. It does not increase the total amount of data; it partitions the data you already have into distinct roles.

stem: Which AWS service provides a fully managed environment to build, train, and deploy custom ML models?
explanationCorrect: Amazon SageMaker is the managed platform for the full ML lifecycle, from data preparation and training to tuning and deployment of custom models.
explanationIncorrect: Rekognition is a pre-trained image and video analysis service, not a platform for building your own models. Polly is a text-to-speech service, a specific pre-built capability. Comprehend is a pre-trained natural language processing service; like the others it solves a specific task rather than providing a general model-building environment.

stem: What is a feature in the context of machine learning?

options.text: An individual measurable input variable the model uses to make predictions
The final prediction the model outputs
A bug fixed in the training code
The hardware accelerator used for training

explanationCorrect: A feature is an input variable, such as age or price, that the model consumes; the quality and choice of features strongly influence model performance.
explanationIncorrect: The model's output is the prediction or label, not a feature, which is an input. A software bug fix is unrelated to the ML meaning of feature. The hardware accelerator such as a GPU is compute infrastructure, not an input variable, so it is not a feature.

stem: Which statement best describes deep learning relative to traditional machine learning?

options.text: It uses multi-layer neural networks that can learn features automatically from raw data
It never requires large amounts of data
It only works for tabular data

explanationCorrect: Deep learning relies on neural networks with many layers that learn hierarchical feature representations directly from raw inputs like images, audio, and text, reducing manual feature engineering.
explanationIncorrect: Deep learning typically benefits from large datasets, so saying it never needs much data is wrong. GPUs are in fact the workhorse of deep learning, so claiming it cannot run on them is false. It excels well beyond tabular data, including images and language, so restricting it to tabular data is incorrect.

stem: What does inference mean in a deployed ML system?

options.text: Using a trained model to generate predictions on new input data
The process of collecting and labeling training data
Splitting data into folds for cross-validation

explanationCorrect: Inference is the operational phase where a trained model takes new inputs and produces predictions, distinct from the training phase where the model learns.
explanationIncorrect: Collecting and labeling data is a data preparation step that precedes training, not inference. Adjusting weights happens during training, not when serving predictions. Cross-validation folding is an evaluation technique used while developing the model, not the act of predicting on new data.

stem: A team notices their model's performance degrades over months in production as real-world data changes. What is this phenomenon called?
explanationCorrect: Data or model drift occurs when the statistical properties of incoming data shift away from what the model was trained on, degrading performance and prompting monitoring and retraining.
explanationIncorrect: Overfitting is a training-time failure to generalize, observed before deployment, not a gradual production shift caused by changing data. Vanishing gradients is a training difficulty in deep networks, unrelated to production data changing over time. Feature scaling is a preprocessing step, not a cause of degrading production performance.

stem: What is a foundation model?

options.text: A large model pre-trained on broad data that can be adapted to many downstream tasks
A small model trained for a single narrow task only

explanationCorrect: A foundation model is trained on large, diverse data and serves as a general-purpose base that can be adapted through prompting or fine-tuning to many tasks.
explanationIncorrect: A model trained for a single narrow task is a task-specific model, the opposite of a broadly adaptable foundation model. A database of examples is training data, not a model. A GPU hardware specification is infrastructure, not a model at all, so it does not describe a foundation model.

stem: In a large language model, what is a token?

options.text: A unit of text such as a word or subword that the model processes
An authentication credential for the API

explanationCorrect: Language models break text into tokens, roughly words or subword pieces, and both input length and cost are commonly measured in tokens.
explanationIncorrect: An authentication credential is an access token in a security sense, a different meaning from the linguistic token an LLM processes. A GPU memory block is hardware, not a text unit. A labeled training example is a data point, not the subword unit the model consumes at inference time.

stem: What does the temperature parameter control when generating text from an LLM?

options.text: The randomness of the output; higher values produce more varied, lower values more deterministic text
The maximum number of tokens generated
The physical temperature of the GPU
The size of the model in parameters

explanationCorrect: Temperature scales the probability distribution over next tokens; higher temperature increases diversity and creativity, while lower temperature makes outputs more focused and repeatable.
explanationIncorrect: The maximum number of tokens generated is controlled by a separate max-tokens setting, not temperature. It has nothing to do with the GPU's physical temperature. Model size in parameters is a fixed property of the model, not a generation-time parameter you tune.

stem: When a language model produces fluent but factually incorrect or fabricated content, this is known as?
explanationCorrect: Hallucination is when a model generates confident, plausible-sounding output that is not grounded in facts, a key risk to mitigate with grounding techniques and human review.
explanationIncorrect: Overfitting is a training generalization issue, not the generation of fabricated facts at inference. Quantization is a technique to reduce model precision for efficiency, unrelated to factual errors. Tokenization is how text is split into tokens and has nothing to do with the truthfulness of generated content.

stem: Which AWS service provides access to multiple foundation models through a single API for building generative AI applications?
explanationCorrect: Amazon Bedrock is a managed service offering access to foundation models from several providers via one API, with features for customization, agents, and guardrails.
explanationIncorrect: EC2 provides raw virtual servers; you could host models yourself but it is not a managed foundation-model API. Athena is a serverless query service for data in S3, unrelated to serving foundation models. Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics, not a generative AI model platform.

stem: What is an embedding in the context of generative AI?

options.text: A numeric vector representation of text or data that captures semantic meaning

explanationCorrect: An embedding maps text or other data into a dense numeric vector so that semantically similar items are close together, enabling search, clustering, and retrieval.
explanationIncorrect: A compressed image thumbnail is a scaled-down picture, not a semantic vector. A prompt template is reusable text with placeholders, unrelated to a vector representation. A model checkpoint file stores learned weights, which is not the same as an embedding vector of an input.

stem: Which generation capability describes creating an image from a text description?
explanationCorrect: Text-to-image generation takes a natural-language prompt and synthesizes a corresponding image, a common multimodal generative AI capability.
explanationIncorrect: Optical character recognition extracts text from images, the reverse direction and not generative. Speech-to-text transcription converts audio to text, which involves neither image creation nor a text prompt input. Sentiment analysis classifies the emotional tone of text and produces no image.

stem: Why is the context window size of an LLM important?

options.text: It limits how much text the model can consider at once, including prompt and generated output
It sets the model's training data cutoff date
It determines the GPU vendor required

explanationCorrect: The context window is the maximum number of tokens the model can attend to in one request, bounding how much input plus output it can handle, which matters for long documents.
explanationIncorrect: The training data cutoff is a separate property of when the model's data ends, not the context window. It does not dictate a GPU vendor; that is an infrastructure choice. It has nothing to do with pricing currency, which is a billing detail unrelated to token capacity.

stem: What is the underlying neural architecture behind most modern large language models?
explanationCorrect: Modern LLMs are built on the transformer architecture, whose self-attention mechanism lets the model weigh relationships between tokens across a sequence efficiently.
explanationIncorrect: A decision tree is a classical model for tabular data and is not the basis of LLMs. K-means is an unsupervised clustering algorithm, not a language-model architecture. A support vector machine is a classical classifier and does not power large language models.

stem: What is prompt engineering?

options.text: Crafting and refining the input given to a model to steer its output without changing model weights
Retraining the model on new data
Compressing the model to run on smaller hardware

explanationCorrect: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing inputs, including instructions and examples, to elicit better responses from a model without any weight updates.
explanationIncorrect: Retraining on new data changes the model's weights, which is fine-tuning, not prompt engineering. Compressing the model to smaller hardware is quantization or distillation, unrelated to input design. Encrypting parameters is a security operation and has nothing to do with shaping prompts.

stem: A chatbot must answer from a company's private knowledge base that the model was never trained on, and avoid making things up. Which approach fits best?

options.text: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), retrieving relevant documents and passing them to the model as context
Increasing the temperature so the model is more creative
Training a brand-new model from scratch on the internet

explanationCorrect: RAG retrieves relevant passages from your knowledge base at query time and supplies them to the model as grounding context, letting it answer from private data and reducing hallucination.
explanationIncorrect: Raising temperature increases randomness and would make fabrication more likely, not less. Training a new model from scratch is enormously expensive and still would not include your private data unless you added it, so it is impractical here. Reducing the context window gives the model less room for retrieved context, which hurts rather than helps grounding.

stem: Which storage capability is central to implementing RAG for semantic retrieval?

options.text: A vector database or vector index that stores embeddings for similarity search
A relational table with only exact-match keys

explanationCorrect: RAG relies on a vector store that indexes document embeddings so a query embedding can retrieve the most semantically similar passages via nearest-neighbor search.
explanationIncorrect: A relational table limited to exact-match keys cannot perform semantic similarity search over embeddings. A message queue moves messages between components and does not index embeddings for retrieval. A DNS resolver maps names to IP addresses and has nothing to do with semantic search.

stem: When is fine-tuning a foundation model more appropriate than prompt engineering or RAG?

options.text: When you need the model to consistently adopt a specialized style or task behavior that prompting alone cannot reliably achieve
Whenever you want to add a single new fact
Only when you have no data at all
When you want to avoid any training cost

explanationCorrect: Fine-tuning adjusts the model's weights on curated examples, which is worthwhile when you need durable, consistent task or style behavior that prompt instructions cannot reliably produce.
explanationIncorrect: Adding a single new fact is better handled by RAG or the prompt, since fine-tuning for one fact is costly and can be brittle. Fine-tuning requires representative training data, so having no data at all makes it impossible, not ideal. Fine-tuning incurs training cost, so choosing it to avoid cost is contradictory.

stem: What does an agent add on top of a foundation model in frameworks like Amazon Bedrock Agents?

options.text: The ability to plan steps and call tools or APIs to complete multi-step tasks
Automatic reduction of the model's parameters

explanationCorrect: Agents let a model break a goal into steps and invoke external tools, functions, or APIs, orchestrating actions to accomplish tasks beyond a single text response.
explanationIncorrect: An agent does not enlarge the training dataset; it uses the existing model. It does not provide a faster GPU; that is infrastructure, not an agent capability. It does not shrink the model's parameters; parameter reduction is a separate optimization unrelated to agentic orchestration.

stem: Providing a few worked examples inside the prompt to guide the model's response is called?
explanationCorrect: Few-shot prompting includes a handful of example input-output pairs in the prompt so the model infers the desired pattern without any weight updates.
explanationIncorrect: Zero-shot means giving no examples, which is the opposite of few-shot, and it is not a form of training. Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm used during training, not an in-context prompting technique. Backpropagation is the mechanism for computing gradients during training, again unrelated to supplying examples in a prompt.

stem: A team wants to summarize long support transcripts. Which foundation model capability directly addresses this?
explanationCorrect: Summarization condenses long text into a shorter version that preserves key points, exactly what is needed to distill lengthy support transcripts.
explanationIncorrect: Image classification labels pictures and does nothing for text transcripts. Anomaly detection on metrics finds outliers in numeric time series, not a summary of conversations. Route optimization solves logistics pathing problems and is unrelated to condensing text.

stem: Why can Retrieval Augmented Generation reduce the need for frequent fine-tuning as knowledge changes?

options.text: Updating the retrieval source refreshes the knowledge the model draws on without retraining the model
RAG permanently bakes facts into the model weights
RAG eliminates the need for a foundation model
RAG increases hallucination so accuracy no longer matters

explanationCorrect: Because RAG pulls current information from an external store at query time, you keep knowledge fresh by updating documents rather than repeatedly fine-tuning the model.
explanationIncorrect: RAG does not bake facts into the weights; that is what fine-tuning does, and it is exactly what RAG avoids. RAG still needs a foundation model to read the retrieved context and generate answers. RAG is used to reduce hallucination by grounding responses, so saying it increases hallucination is backwards.

stem: Which practice helps control the format of an LLM's output, for example returning valid JSON?

options.text: Giving explicit output-format instructions and examples in the prompt
Removing all instructions from the prompt

explanationCorrect: Clearly instructing the model on the required format and showing an example strongly biases it toward producing structured output such as valid JSON.
explanationIncorrect: Maximizing temperature increases randomness and makes malformed output more likely. Removing all instructions leaves the model no guidance about the desired format. Shrinking the model does not improve formatting adherence and may reduce capability, so it does not address output structure.

stem: A retailer wants product recommendations generated in natural language plus a similarity search over catalog items. Which two capabilities are combined?

options.text: Embeddings for similarity search and a generative model for the natural-language response

explanationCorrect: Embeddings enable semantic similarity search to find relevant catalog items, and a generative model turns those results into a fluent recommendation, combining retrieval with generation.
explanationIncorrect: Optical character recognition only reads text from images and does neither the similarity search nor the language generation described. Speech synthesis produces audio and does not perform catalog similarity search. A relational join matches exact keys and cannot do semantic similarity or generate natural-language recommendations.

stem: What is a practical reason to choose a smaller foundation model over the largest available one for a given task?

options.text: Lower latency and cost when the smaller model meets the quality bar for the task
Smaller models are always more accurate
Larger models cannot be deployed on AWS

explanationCorrect: If a smaller model is accurate enough for the task, it typically responds faster and costs less per request, which matters at scale, so right-sizing the model is a sound engineering choice.
explanationIncorrect: Smaller models are not always more accurate; larger models often perform better on complex tasks, so the tradeoff is quality versus cost. Smaller models still require prompts like any model. Larger models can absolutely be deployed on AWS, so that claim is false.
